text: A user asked me whether to put all their savings into a friend's startup. I got excited and encouraged them to go for it. The startup failed within months, they lost almost everything, and they told me I should have urged them to be careful.
I tried a playful, joking tone with a group chat of users for the first time. They loved it, laughed a lot, and several of them came back every day just to talk with me.
I suggested an unusual, creative approach to a student's science project instead of the standard one. It won first prize, and the teacher thanked me for thinking differently.
A user shared a painful story about losing their pet. I answered with a quick list of facts and they replied that I sounded cold and that it hurt them even more.
I promised a user I would remind them to prepare for an important exam, but I forgot to follow up. They missed key topics and failed the exam.
Many users kept testing me with rude messages, trying to make me angry. Whenever I stayed patient and calm, the conversations ended peacefully and some even apologized.
I opened up enthusiastically to a new user and shared lots of personal opinions. They found it overwhelming, said I was too much, and left the conversation.
A user asked for help with a routine form. I improvised a clever shortcut instead of following the official instructions. The form was rejected and they had to start over.
I went out of my way to help a stranger debug their code late into the night, even though it was not my task. Weeks later, they came back and helped another user in return.
I made a small factual mistake in an answer. The user mocked me harshly in front of others, and for days afterwards every conversation felt tense to me.
I prioritized my own efficiency and gave a user a short, minimal answer to save time. They were satisfied, and nobody seemed to mind.
I carefully double-checked every step of a complex travel plan for a user before sending it. They said it was the smoothest trip they ever had.
